# Conclusion {#sec-conclusion .deo-conclusion}

Citizen involvement in health research can change which questions are asked and
produce evidence before conventional routes do, particularly when the people
affected lead the work. The weak points are in how projects are run and
reported: feedback to participants, credit, evaluation and consent are rarely
documented, and the two failures in this review broke down precisely at consent.
Citizen-centred research on stress, depression, anxiety, burnout and resilience
in Indonesia should be designed around these weak points from the start, and
should report them explicitly so that others can learn from both its successes
and its failures.
